Reportedly, Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, indicating that this cooling technology will play a more important role in its future hardware product lineup. Details below.

Apple is betting bigger on vapor chamber cooling technology

Weibo tipster account "定焦數碼" posted that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber orders," and speculated that the move is "likely to prepare more powerful cooling solutions for its first foldable iPhone and next year's anniversary edition model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address overheating issues that had persisted across several previous generations.

A vapor chamber works by evaporating a small amount of liquid near a heat source, then condensing it at a cooler location, spreading the heat over a larger area before letting the liquid flow back to repeat the cycle.

To see the whole process in action, check out this great video from Know Art:

Although the Weibo post speculates that Apple's increased procurement this time is to prepare for the iPhone Ultra and the rumored anniversary edition iPhone launching in 2027, looking at the timeline, it would be more reasonable for this year's product lineup to adopt the technology first.

Apple has reportedly asked suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, up from the previous target of 7 to 8 million units. At the same time, the company has also stockpiled around 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

Along with the increased orders, there are also reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and yield issues, clearing the way to ramp up production ahead of the September launch.
